faq.question: What are the eligibility criteria and prerequisites for this course?
faq.answer: Basic computer literacy, comfortable web browsing, and familiarity with digital productivity tools (Google Docs, web browsers) are the only prerequisites. You do NOT need any prior coding, programming (HTML/CSS/JS/PHP), or technical web development experience. Learners of all educational backgrounds can enroll directly.

faq.question: Do I need to know how to code to succeed as a No-Code Website Professional?
faq.answer: No. The entire curriculum is designed around modern visual development platforms (WordPress Site Editor/Elementor, Framer, and Webflow). You will learn visual layout principles, the CSS Box Model, Flexbox, and CSS Grid visually through interactive design panels rather than by writing raw syntax code.

faq.question: What is the course duration and total guided instructional commitment?
faq.answer: The course spans 3 Months and comprises exactly 120 Guided Instructional Hours across 9 structured curriculum modules, supplemented by recommended laboratory studio practice and portfolio project assembly.

faq.question: Why does the course teach both WordPress Block Editor and Elementor?
faq.answer: WordPress powers over 40% of the web. Modern WordPress 6.7+ utilizes Block Themes and Full Site Editing (FSE) for ultra-fast, lightweight websites, while Elementor remains the dominant visual builder in digital marketing agencies and freelancing ecosystems. Learning both ensures you can handle modern native block builds as well as agency Elementor client retainers.

faq.question: How thoroughly is Framer covered in this program?
faq.answer: Framer is covered in depth across 24 guided instructional hours (Module 04). You will master Framer's visual canvas, Stacks, CSS Grids, interactive component variants, 60fps spring scroll physics, native CMS collections, native forms, Framer AI Agents, and free staging deployment on .framer.website subdomains.

faq.question: What makes Webflow training in this course professional and agency-grade?
faq.answer: Rather than teaching haphazard drag-and-drop styling, Module 05 teaches Webflow using the industry-standard Finsweet Client-First naming methodology. You will learn semantic HTML5 tagging (<header>, <nav>, <section>, <main>, <footer>), rem-based spacing scales, relational CMS database architecture, and custom Interactions 2.0 micro-animations.

faq.question: Is Figma taught as part of this web development curriculum?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 02 is dedicated to Figma-to-Web foundations. You will learn 12-column layout grids, typography scales, color token libraries, Auto Layout nesting (which directly maps to CSS Flexbox), low-to-high fidelity responsive wireframing, and production asset export (WebP, SVG).

faq.question: How does the course ensure websites look good across all devices?
faq.answer: Responsive design is taught as a foundational discipline across every platform. You will master desktop-down cascading inheritance, viewport breakpoints (desktop, tablet, mobile), fluid sizing units (rem, vw, %), and conduct mandatory testing across real device widths down to 320px to prevent horizontal overflow.

faq.question: What is the mandatory responsive header requirement in Module 04?
faq.answer: In Module 04, every student must engineer a functional responsive website header in Framer. On desktop, it displays inline navigation links and a primary CTA. On mobile viewports, it dynamically transitions into a branded logo and an animated hamburger icon that opens a functional full-screen or dropdown navigation drawer.

faq.question: How are lead forms and automated workflows handled?
faq.answer: In Module 07, you learn to configure native website forms with client-side field validation, anti-spam protections (honeypots, Cloudflare Turnstile), and connect form webhooks to Make.com (with Zapier comparisons) to log submissions automatically into Google Sheets and trigger instant email alerts.

faq.question: What technical SEO and analytics tools are covered?
faq.answer: You will implement complete on-page technical SEO: unique page titles, meta descriptions, semantic heading hierarchies, descriptive image alt text, auto-generated XML sitemaps, canonical tags, and 301 redirects. You will also install Google Analytics 4 (GA4) measurement IDs, configure `generate_lead` conversion events, and verify indexing in Google Search Console.

faq.question: Do I need to buy expensive web hosting to take this course?
faq.answer: No. Under our Zero-Cost Learning Policy, all coursework, lab assignments, and portfolio capstone projects are completed using 100% free environments: LocalWP (free desktop local server), Framer Free Plan (free .framer.website staging subdomain), and Webflow Starter Workspace (free .webflow.io staging subdomain). No web hosting purchases are required for students.

faq.question: Are live custom domain names (.com, .in) provided with the course?
faq.answer: No. Live custom domains and production cloud hosting are client-funded operational expenses. Students deploy, test, and defend their portfolio websites on free public staging subdomains (.framer.website and .webflow.io) and LocalWP archives, exactly as professional agencies do during client staging phases.

faq.question: Will I need to pay for premium Elementor, Framer, or Webflow subscriptions?
faq.answer: No. All required course competencies, exercises, and assessed portfolio deliverables operate strictly within the free tiers of Framer, Webflow, and LocalWP/WordPress. Any advanced features demonstrated by instructors (such as Elementor Pro Theme Builder) are for educational exposure and have approved free-tier alternatives.

faq.question: What are Framer AI Agents and Framer MCP, and how are they taught?
faq.answer: Framer AI Agents assist with initial layout ideation, copy drafting, and style remixing. Framer MCP (officially launched Oct 22, 2026) enables AI visual agents to interact with design canvases. We teach these tools strictly from visual user interfaces for productivity acceleration; zero backend server coding or custom MCP development is required.

faq.question: What are the capabilities and limitations of Webflow AI Site Builder?
faq.answer: Webflow AI accelerates preliminary structural scaffolding and content drafting. However, students are explicitly taught that Webflow AI has restrictions on pre-existing non-AI projects, and AI-generated code components require paid plans. All student layouts are manually refactored into clean Client-First structures without custom coding.

faq.question: Which generative AI visual tools are used, and can the images be used commercially?
faq.answer: We utilize Adobe Firefly and Canva AI for generating website hero backgrounds, textures, and visual mockups. Students learn prompt engineering, generative fill, aspect-ratio expansion, WebP compression, and adhere to commercial licensing standards (ensuring assets are commercially safe for client delivery).

faq.question: What are the three assessed portfolio projects I will build?

faq.question: How is this course different from E-Commerce Website Mastery?
faq.answer: No-Code Website Professional focuses on marketing websites, business hubs, lead-generation pages, and dynamic content CMS architectures using WordPress, Framer, and Webflow. lessons.lesson_title: Web Accessibility Standards (WCAG 2.2) & Lighthouse Auditing
lessons.what_is_taught: Web accessibility fundamentals: understanding WCAG 2.2 Level AA compliance; keyboard navigation accessibility: testing full site navigation using only the `Tab`, `Shift+Tab`, `Enter`, and `Escape` keys; visible focus indicator styling; color contrast remediation: testing text contrast ratios against backgrounds (minimum 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text); auditing image alternative text for screen readers; respecting user motion preferences via the `prefers-reduced-motion` media query; running Google Lighthouse audits in Chrome DevTools; interpreting Core Web Vitals metrics: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), Interaction to Next Paint (INP), and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS); using the WAVE accessibility evaluation extension for rapid issue remediation.
subtopics: WCAG 2.2 AA principles: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, and Robust (POUR) design fundamentals
Keyboard accessibility: ensuring logical tab order through navigation, cards, and forms without keyboard traps
Focus indicator design: styling prominent, high-contrast focus rings for keyboard users rather than removing outlines
Color contrast remediation: testing foreground text against background colors using contrast analyzers and adjusting lightness values
Accessible media: auditing decorative images (empty alt tags) vs informational images (descriptive semantic alt text)
Reduced motion safeguards: disabling high-intensity parallax and autoplay animations when users enable reduced motion in OS settings
Lighthouse performance & accessibility audits: running synthetic audits and scoring >90 in Accessibility, Best Practices, and SEO
Core Web Vitals optimization: eliminating layout shifts (CLS) by assigning explicit width/height dimensions to images
lessons.why_it_matters: Building accessible websites is not only an ethical and legal imperative; accessible websites rank higher on search engines and provide superior usability for all visitors.
lessons.what_learner_does: Audits a website using the WAVE tool and Chrome Lighthouse, identifies 5 accessibility defects (contrast, focus, alt tags), remediates them, and re-tests to achieve a >90 Lighthouse score.
lessons.expected_outcome: A Web Accessibility Compliance Report with before-and-after contrast test evidence and an official Google Lighthouse score report exceeding 90.
lessons.example: Adjusting light-grey body text (#888888) on a white background to dark charcoal (#222222) to achieve an accessible 10.5:1 contrast ratio.
